title: Crucifixion of Jesus and the Demonic Opposition Framework
description: The crucifixion of Jesus of Nazareth established the foundational Christian narrative of cosmic conflict between divine and demonic forces. Early Christian theology interpreted Jesus's execution as a victory over Satan and demonic powers (Colossians 2:15), framing the crucifixion within a cosmic drama of spiritual warfare. This theological framework, developed extensively by Paul and subsequent church fathers, provided the conceptual infrastructure for later Christian demonology by establishing that demonic powers were real, active in the world, and opposed to divine order. The narrative of demonic opposition — and its conquest through Christ — became the theological grounding for centuries of thinking about witches as agents of Satan.
historiographical_note: Stuart Clark's intellectual history in Thinking with Demons traces how the demonic opposition framework embedded in early Christian theology ultimately shaped early modern demonological theory. The cosmic dualism of Christ vs. Satan provided the template within which witchcraft as diabolical pact became theologically coherent.
source_method: Biblical and patristic texts; secondary scholarship on early Christian theology
